_comment: IPC -> BNS mapping, source-audited 2026-08-16. Direction is old->new ONLY. Every section number and every kind in this file was read this session out of published tables, not recalled: the NCRB / UP Police 'Corresponding Section Table of BNS 2023', the Delhi Police Academy BNS Handbook (Section B, Annexure I new sections, Annexure III deleted sections), the BPRD / Maharaja Ranjit Singh Punjab Police Academy BNS handbook comparative chart, and the bare Act 45 of 2023 on India Code, which supplies every BNS section heading. verified_by is stamped ONLY where two independent sources agree on BOTH section numbers AND the kind; where they diverge, or only one covers the question, verified_by stays null and the row is INERT - Mapping.require_verified refuses it until an operator rules. A null row is not a wrong row: for most of them the two comparative tables agree on the numbers and only the one_to_one/changed call lacks a second vote. See audit-report.md for the per-row citations, the conflict list and the corrections made to the previous starter file. kind: one_to_one = the offence is carried across with no source flagging a substantive change; changed = two or more sources flag altered ingredients, scope or punishment; new_offence = null old side; deleted = null new side. new_section names the SECTION, not the punishment sub-clause; sub-clause detail lives in notes. Many-to-one is legal (IPC 499 and 500 both land on BNS 356), and the reverse lookup returns None rather than guessing.
